P1.reason: B separates roles, marking, board update, turn order and winning lines/end; A lumps the whole game into one undivided group, naming no rules.

differences.reason: Hurts: one group of everything is not a division into rules at all.
Helps: winning lines, game end and goals form the recognizable 'three in a row wins' rule.
Helps: board setup and how cells persist or change; mixes init with update, slightly broad.
Helps: marking a blank cell on your turn, with its effect; a clear move rule.
Helps: turn alternation with x moving first is a distinct, nameable rule.
Helps slightly: the two players; small but legitimate setup element.
Neutral to slight help: diagonals as subrule; redundant with B1 but harmless.
